introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklets are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One Hour): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION II (30 minutes) - DATA ANALYSIS**

In an experiment to investigate how pressure, $P$, varies with altitude, $h$, in the troposphere, a research physicist obtained the following values.

| $P$ / kPa | $h$ / m |
|---|---|
| 82.11 | 1500 |
| 71.39 | 2500 |
| 53.94 | 4502 |
| 46.74 | 5505 |
| 36.71 | 7250 |
| 30.82 | 8500 |
| 28.73 | 9000 |

The equation relating $P$ and $h$ is $P = P_0e^{-\beta h}$ where $\beta$ and $P_0$ are constants.
incertitudes: Question 7 : le sujet n'imprime pas de total ; les marques imprimées (9 + 8 + 3) donnent 20, utilisé pour `points` de l'exercice. Marques par bloc : (a)(i) 9 et (a)(ii) 8 (donc a = 17), (b) 3.

Question 7 : le graphe (a)(i) est à tracer par le candidat ; le corrigé donne la grandeur à porter en ordonnée ($\ln (P/\mathrm{kPa})$ contre $h$), le tableau des valeurs, les échelles et la lecture. Les sept points sont presque parfaitement alignés (coefficient de corrélation -0.99999) ; le point h = 5505 m est le plus écarté de la droite d'ajustement (écart de 0.002 sur ln P). Résultats : beta = 1.40e-4 par m, P0 = 101 kPa (101.3 kPa).

Question 7(b) : le sujet dit « mean molar mass of the predominant ions is 28.9 g » : lu comme une masse molaire de 28.9 g/mol, donc m = 28.9e-3 / 6.02e23 = 4.80e-26 kg par molécule (le mot « ions » est impropre pour les molécules de l'air). Constantes non imprimées : N_A = 6.02e23 /mol, g = 9.8 m/s2, T = 288 K. On obtient k = 1.17e-23 J/K, inférieur à la constante de Boltzmann admise (1.38e-23 J/K) : les données imprimées correspondent à une échelle de hauteur 1/beta = 7.1 km, plus courte que celle d'une atmosphère isotherme à 288 K (8.4 km) ; le corrigé donne la valeur déduite des données et le signale.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Plot a suitable graph to determine the value of $P_0$ and $\beta$. *[9 marks]*

(ii) Determine the values of $P_0$ and $\beta$. *[8 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Choosing the graph.** Take natural logarithms of $P = P_0e^{-\beta h}$:
$$\ln P = \ln P_0 - \beta h.$$
This has the form $y = mx + c$ with $y = \ln P$ and $x = h$. So plot **$\ln(P/\mathrm{kPa})$ (vertical axis) against $h/\mathrm{m}$ (horizontal axis)**: a straight line with **gradient $= -\beta$** and **intercept on the vertical axis $= \ln P_0$**.

**Table of values** (to be calculated by the candidate):

| $h$ / m | 1500 | 2500 | 4502 | 5505 | 7250 | 8500 | 9000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P$ / kPa | 82.11 | 71.39 | 53.94 | 46.74 | 36.71 | 30.82 | 28.73 |
| $\ln(P/\mathrm{kPa})$ | 4.408 | 4.268 | 3.988 | 3.845 | 3.603 | 3.428 | 3.358 |

**The graph (to be drawn by the candidate).** Axes labelled $h/\mathrm{m}$ and $\ln(P/\mathrm{kPa})$, with the horizontal axis starting at $0$ so that the intercept can be read (for example $0$ to $9000\ \mathrm{m}$ with $1000\ \mathrm{m}$ per large square; vertical axis from $3.0$ to $4.8$ with $0.2$ per large square), scales using more than half of each axis, all seven points plotted accurately. The points lie very close to a single straight line **sloping downwards**; a best-fit line is drawn through them and **extended to the vertical axis** at $h = 0$.

**(ii) Values of $P_0$ and $\beta$.** Use a large triangle on the best-fit line, for example the points $(1500\ \mathrm{m},\ 4.408)$ and $(9000\ \mathrm{m},\ 3.358)$:
$$\text{gradient} = \frac{3.358 - 4.408}{9000 - 1500} = \frac{-1.050}{7500} = -1.40\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^{-1}}.$$

$$\boxed{\beta = 1.40\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^{-1}}}$$

Intercept at $h = 0$: $\ln P_0 = 4.408 + 1.40\times10^{-4}\times1500 = 4.618$, so
$$P_0 = e^{4.618} = 101\ \mathrm{kPa}\ (101.3\ \mathrm{kPa}),$$
which is the value of atmospheric pressure at sea level.

Check on a measured point: $P = 101.3\,e^{-1.40\times10^{-4}\times9000} = 101.3\times0.2837 = 28.7\ \mathrm{kPa}$, as in the table. (A least-squares fit of the seven points gives gradient $-1.400\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and $P_0 = 101.3\ \mathrm{kPa}$.)

**$\beta = 1.40\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and $P_0 \approx 101\ \mathrm{kPa}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that the average temperature of the troposphere is $15\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and the mean molar mass of the predominant ions is $28.9\ \mathrm{g}$, determine the value for $k$ given that $\beta = \dfrac{mg}{kT}$ where $m$ is mass of a molecule, $T$ is the mean absolute temperature of the ions and $g$ the gravitational field strength. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Constants (not printed in the paper): $N_A = 6.02\times10^{23}\ \mathrm{mol^{-1}}$ and $g = 9.8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

Mass of one molecule: $m = \dfrac{M}{N_A} = \dfrac{28.9\times10^{-3}}{6.02\times10^{23}} = 4.80\times10^{-26}\ \mathrm{kg}$.

Absolute temperature: $T = 15 + 273 = 288\ \mathrm{K}$.

Rearranging $\beta = \dfrac{mg}{kT}$ and using $\beta = 1.40\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^{-1}}$ from part (a):
$$k = \frac{mg}{\beta T} = \frac{4.80\times10^{-26}\times9.8}{1.40\times10^{-4}\times288} = \frac{4.70\times10^{-25}}{4.03\times10^{-2}} = 1.17\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}.$$

**$k \approx 1.2\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$** ($1.17\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$): the Boltzmann constant as deduced from these data. It is somewhat below the accepted value of $1.38\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, because the model assumes an isothermal atmosphere at $288\ \mathrm{K}$ whereas the real troposphere cools with altitude.
